firmwares.description: M-VAVE's own stock firmware V15 (DX7-style FM synth), published under Apache-2.0 in m-vave/fm1_open: the way back to stock.
The custom firmware the others build on: the FM-1's own synth engines, a sequencer, effects and a better panel, with an editor in the browser.

A karaoke robot with a band: it sings songs from karaoke and MIDI files, or lines you type, to the notes you play. Its face is the voice. Keys, bass and drums play along, with a step sequencer and sixteen punch-in effects.
A generative ambient machine after Music for Airports: it plays itself from the start, breathing voices, bells on tape loops of unequal length, a gliding bass. You do not perform it, you tend it.

Dark ambient drones and feedback screams from the frozen tundra. Built on GR!MM, with HOWL, a feedback-loop voice after the Synthux Audrey II that wakes out of silence and grows into a howl, and 46 arctic sounds.
A tracker for the FM-1: patterns written top to bottom, step by step, with note, instrument, chord and effect columns, the way trackers have always worked.

A generative Berlin School MIDI sequencer: voices that repeat, phase on loops of unequal length and earn their mutations over time. The FM-1 makes no sound itself: each voice goes out over USB on its own MIDI channel to your synths.

A six-track groovebox written from scratch: TR drums from Plaits' 808 and 909 models, a sampler with a 16-slice slicer, a bass and three free tracks (analog, 6-op FM, 303 acid), scenes and fills, all at 44.1 kHz.

Generative ambient: four editable layers from 64 sound recipes, 24 worlds, 24 motifs and 32 scales. GROW varies the phrases, seven EVOLVE processes change them over time. Felucca's sound pages stay. Built on Felucca 1.6.1.
A bytebeat synth: play one-line formulas, tweak them with the knobs, and write your own, with a random button in the formula creator that is really fun. A beta, built on Dinghy.

Felucca continued: a multi-engine synth with ANALOG, SEM, HADES, PHASE, TRIO, a tonewheel, FM6, physical models, voices, samples, grain and slices, drums, noise and an experimental DRONE engine. Pair Morph blends two engines, a HOME screen of your own and free macros a track for live sound design.

A dual-timbral wavetable synth after Carnac's standing stones: 15 morphing wavetable banks, seven voice architectures, a MAQ 16/3-style sequencer for modulated sequences and a chord sequencer for progressions, spring, tomb and tank reverbs. Its own installer also writes its wavetables. Built on X0X and Felucca.

A chiptune groovebox with replicas of the NES, Game Boy and Sega Master System sound chips, in three views: RACK for the 16 steps of a page, CHIP to set up each channel, SONG to chain the pages into a song.
A Telepathic Orchid-style chord instrument: one hand plays roots, the other shapes chords; voicings, performance modes, bass and a looper.

A deep synth grown out of SLOOP: 23 engines and 407 sounds, from HYBRID (three oscillators, two filters, a mod matrix) to six-operator FM, wavetables, wave sequencing, a Juno and physical models; arp, step sequencer, MPE and a web editor for every parameter.

Chords after the Orchid, with controls made for the FM-1: one key plays a chord with a bass note. Also 27 scales, an arpeggiator, a sequencer with drums and a song mode, and a pixel flower that grows as you play.
A Yamaha CS-80 in spirit: eight voices of two channels, high- and low-pass filters in series, ring modulator, the touch response and 22 tones from the owner's manual. A sound module played over MIDI.
A MIDI controller: notes in any scale with its chords on the black keys, four banks of knobs, an arpeggiator and Euclidean drums, with General MIDI sounds of its own when nothing is connected.

A beat dojo for scratch DJs and beatmakers: boom bap, lo-fi and breaks from 16 rhythm families with swing and fills, an eight-lane 32-step sequencer, punch-in effects you record bar by bar, a bass voice. Sound banks and editor in the browser.

A rhythm box of ceremony percussion: djembe, cajon, udu, clapsticks, maracas and triangle, their real strokes on the black keys, a step sequencer on the white keys and 31 rhythms from the literature. Played alone: a berimbau with its caxixi, a buzzing tanpura and a breathing shruti box. Built on fm1-base.

Your base for your own FM-1 or SMK-37 firmware: everything under it done and documented (updates, USB rescue, MIDI over USB and the TRS jack with clock, USB audio, keys, screen, flash storage, an update screen), a 4-voice sine on top, tests and a CI that releases with attestation. Fork it, replace the sine.

An ambient instrument for live sessions: warm synths, spacious pads and delicate plucks over a generative Euclidean sequencer on one track, with delays and reverbs from spring to shimmer. Built on Felucca.

A generative dub techno machine that plays itself from the moment it is on: chord stabs into a tape echo, FM pings, a sub bass on five grooves, a ducking kick, crackle, and an eight-bar arrangement with breaks and fills.
A multimorphing bitimbral synthesizer: two complete parts, three ways to play them together, and a morph that glides between two versions of every sound.

A groovebox for lively mediæval dance music: hurdy-gurdy, lutes, shawms and frame drums over drones, four tracks with 64-step sequencers, mediæval modes and temperaments, and velocity from the FM-1's own keys. Built on GHOULBOX and Felucca.
Draw the sound: a waveform drawn and changed with the knobs, saved, morphed into another one, and a third waveform modulating the result.
A bard's instrument for LARP, medieval and high fantasy: recorder, hurdy-gurdy, harp and a tavern kit on four tracks, encounters and songs for the table. "Mother Melody hears thy song."
A questionable musical instrument: ten artisanal farts, reverb, delay and a sixteen-step sequencer.
Felucca 1.5.1 with eight sequences a track to switch between and chain one after another; the user samples are left out to make room.
Felucca with a hardware-inspired Studio in the browser (play it there without an FM-1): many engines, presets, skins. A beta.
A physically modelled kalimba: tines laid out like the real one, thumb-roll chords, mbira patterns, a sound hole to cover, grains, tape and a plate reverb. Play it in the browser first.

A groovebox around one engine, ChoralRoot's FM TONE: eight tracks, p-locks and preset sound locks, conditions, ratchets, chords, and MIDI FX for generative patterns and for reworking the ones you have.
One piece on the FM-1: Chopin's Étude Op. 10 No. 1 on a sampled Steinway D. It plays the étude, lets you shape it with rubato, touch and accents, practise it and move it. Built on Tuna and Felucca.
Doom on the FM-1: one FreeDM arena on the keys and a knob, synthesised sound effects.
A C64 SID chip on the FM-1: tune player (reSID), GoatTracker editor and a 12-instrument synth.
The Juno-106 emulation of KR-106 ported to the FM-1: six voices on both cores, the BBD stereo chorus, 128 factory presets and a 1980s Roland look.

A pixel-art RPG while you make music, built on SLOOP: four heroes, one a track, walk through a village and fight monsters and bosses as your loop plays, every SLOOP screen redrawn in the game's style.
A chord machine after the HiChord, with extras: chords in a key under the white keys, slash chords and inversions, sounds, envelopes, effects and a looper.
One firmware, many synths: CS-1, Scintilla and OberVave as modules in flash; HOME opens the picker.
A General MIDI sequencer with 16 tracks, 128 General MIDI instruments to choose from and a drum kit (on track 10). It can store up to 64 songs, each containing up to 128 measures.
Mellotron-style tape sounds, coloured with effects and lo-fi tape: flutes, strings and choirs as on the old tape frames, played from the keys.
A three-oscillator monosynth in the spirit of the classic Moogs: a 24 dB/octave ladder filter, two contours, 100 factory patches, an arpeggiator, a sequencer and MIDI. Built on Felucca.
A drum machine in the classic step-grid style: voices after the 909, 808, 707, 606, DMX and more, a machine per voice, accents and patterns. Play it in the browser first.
A chord harp inspired by the Omnichord: strum the white keys, pick chords on the black ones.

An ambient drone and texture instrument: tap a key to latch a drone, a note or a chord in your key, press to swell it. Three layers a voice into a big reverb with shimmer and freeze; GLINT plays icy FM bells on top, by hand, by arpeggiator or a 32-step sequencer, and BASS holds a deep note below.

An electric piano, vibraphone and marimba, physically modelled, no samples, with drive, tremolo or wah, phaser, chorus, delay and reverb (hall, plate, infinite), tap tempo and MIDI clock sync, an arpeggiator, a sequencer, scales and presets.

A shigin conductor after the Suiko ST-50: its two rows of keys, the key set in honsū, equal or its own just tuning, a koto and twelve more sounds on a 6-op FM engine, ring time, vibrato, trill and a looper.

A monophonic macro-oscillator on the open Plaits DSP: all 24 models with harmonics, timbre and morph, an 8-slot mod matrix fed by an envelope, two LFOs, velocity, aftertouch and random, a low-pass gate, and a DRONE mode.
Dungeon synth: a cathedral hall reverb, tape and crush, a hurdy-gurdy engine, choirs, organs and recorded psaltery and harp, an old-RPG screen with wall torches.
One analog-style synth laid out like the classic microKORG, with a screen that draws the sound.

Golana's synth with a sequencer for whole songs: 64 steps a pattern, 32 programs (up to 2,048 steps), a SONGMODE that plays from a first to a last program once or on repeat, and USB MIDI out to sequence other synths.

Dark ambient, dungeon synth and deathdream: four tracks, seven sound sources from VA and 6-op FM to formant voices and physical models, tape, granular freeze and reverbs up to infinite, a 64-step sequencer and song mode. Built on Dinghy.
A chord and string instrument: 16 synthesized sounds, 50 chord styles, editable voicings, guitar tunings, and Freeplay, Strum and Arp modes with partial-chord pulses.

A chord groovebox after the Roland J-6: 100 chord sets, 9 phrase styles with 12 variations each and a 64-pattern step sequencer, on a four-voice Juno-style synth from Clipper with chorus, delay and reverb. A chord map on the screen shows which chord sits on which key. Built on Dinghy.
A drum machine: eight tracks of drums, a step sequencer, Grids, a pumping compressor, LFOs, resonators and live effects. Play it in the browser first.

Hypnotic techno and acid: a breathing pad, a deep drone, a generative 303 line and grain over drums you sequence. Flip patterns on the bar, break it down, build it up. Forked from AMB-1. One of a pack of four: LOF-1 (a lofi groovebox), ECO-1 (a plant plays it) and GRAV-1 (a star and its planets), experimental, on its project page.
A six-voice JUNO-60 style polysynth with chorus, arpeggiator and a 16-step recorder.
Dark, industrial, Brazilian: drones that breathe, ten engines (6-op FM, a superwave analog with a ladder filter), four tracks, a mod matrix, live effects.

A bio-synthetic groovebox: six tracks drawn as living beings in thermal colours, eight engines (FM6 with Dexed, analog, phase, voice…), mutating macros, song mode from SLOOP. Not yet tested much on a real FM-1.

A pocket tracker for any style: six tracks with an engine each (pulse, 4-bit wave, noise, 6-operator FM, drum kit or sample), patterns chained into a song, 32 live effects and tools that write beats for you. A beta, not yet tried on a real FM-1 by its maker.
A tracker in the LSDJ / picoTracker / M8 line: song, chain and phrase screens, instruments, effects and a mixer, on the FM-1's own keys and screen.

Four synth and sampler tracks and a drum track on 14 engines, among them wavetable, 6-op FM, tape scrub, granular and a slicer; a 64-step sequencer, a chord progression generator, macros and sidechain ducking.
A groovebox inspired by the OP-XY: eight tracks on nine engines, step tricks and locks, weave, a conductor and throws.

A generative groovebox in the style of early-90s PC tracker music: six lanes (lead, arp, pad, bass, drums, sfx) composed live in ten S3M-scene styles. You mix styles instead of programming steps. Built on Tuna and Felucca.

An ambience machine for DJ interludes: switch it on and a random world in key plays, four parts, buttons that are verbs, and the worlds you like breed new ones. Clock follow. Play it in the browser first.
A modular synth you patch in the browser: modules (oscillators, filters, envelopes, delays) nest into assemblies you save and reuse, and the patch plays on the FM-1, polyphonic with a Voicing module.
An original four-part groovebox with a 1990s workflow: three melodic parts and a 16-lane drum part, 128 melodic presets, eight drum kits, song arrangement, an arpeggiator and recorded knob moves.
Total playing pleasure, far beyond Felucca: recording without quantize, microtonal scales, a Casio CZ-1, a bit-by-bit Dexed, scale modes made for an MPC Sample as its companion.
A MIDI monitor for USB, the TRS jack and Bluetooth (as device and host at once): hex or words, filters, stats. Its THRU routes, each filtered, make the FM-1 a Bluetooth MIDI dongle.
A tiny minimalist ensemble after Philip Glass: it starts playing when you switch on, you join whenever you like. In EASY mode every white key is a chord that fits. Four models, twenty pieces.
Felucca with six tracks and new engines: SID, Braids' 48 models, a TB-303 and engines after Elektron's Analog Four, SY Chip and Digitone 2, a ping-pong delay and a new reverb. Built on Felucca 1.5.

Six monophonic tracks of synth and FX machines, pages of eight knobs, a filter and a tape delay on every track, three LFOs a track, parameter locks and slides. Forked from Hortator, with sounds ported from MONO2K.

A semi-modular drone synth played like a Kaoss Pad: four oscillators modulating each other through eight routings, and keys that move a cursor on an XY pad instead of playing notes: white keys are points, black keys gestures. ARP, a polymetric sequencer, a clock in Hz and eight generative environments.
Twelve singers, from Jerry the monk to Snider the punk, each in its own voice: MonkSynth's formant voices, played with velocity and pressure from the FM-1's own keys.

Six mono machines in the spirit of Elektron's Monomachine: FM, superwaves, wavetables, a SID, a voice and four drum synths, one per track. A 64-step sequencer with parameter locks, trig conditions and ratchets, a lofi bus, four demo parts and a web patch editor.
A monosynth: one voice with analogue-modelled oscillators and five filters (ladder, diode ladder, OTA, Sallen-Key, state-variable), unison, chorus, delay and reverb, and 14 presets.

A sad wavetable synth played by a pixel blob in a rainy room: its eyes are the filter, its mouth the envelope, its tears the delay. Toy-keyboard accompaniment with 13 gloomy beats, auto-bass, arpeggiator, loop recorder.
A pattern sequencer after Reason's Matrix: up to four channels of MIDI sequence data out, and a few voices built in to build the patterns with.

A generative instrument after a small modular setup: six freely assignable tracks, 12 engines (selected Plaits, Rings and Elements algorithms and voices of its own), 224 tones and 76 Biomes, a mixer with shared effects, 16-step phrases and named User Banks. Plays and edits live in the browser.
Forest, Psytrance, Goa and Hitech grooves, built on Felucca and SLOOP: original drums and icons and four factory songs. A test release: not yet fully tested on the device.
A drone synth: two drifting virtual-analog drones, each with its own part, swells, LFOs, effects and a sequencer.
A space adventure while you make music, built on SLOOP 2.7.1: fly between planets with two knobs, land, mine, fight sentinels and warp between stars, every SLOOP screen floating over the game.
Felucca with randomization as a ritual: every new sound summons one of 30 demons of the Ars Goetia, its sigil takes the screen and its rank decides how wild the sound gets.

An 8-voice analog-style poly in the spirit of the classic American polys of 1979-84, now on four tracks: each its own sound, arp and sequence; a mixer with chorus, delay, plate reverb and drive sends, a master with DJ filter and compressor. Tracks start on the bar, patterns keep their sounds.
The Sega Genesis / Mega Drive's Yamaha YM2612: six channels of 4-operator FM. Its web app takes patches from game music (VGM) and OPM files and streams VGM tunes to the FM-1 to play.
A four-track groovebox: three synths and a drum machine in a colour-coded Synth, Drum, Event Tape and Mixer workflow, loops turned into songs, user macros, screens after the OP-1. Based on SLOOP.

A generative groovebox you perform on: ten genres of self-playing pieces, an auto-DJ with breakdowns, builds and drops, Euclidean drums, an acid line that answers itself, beat FX and DX7-style FM voices from your own .syx.

An old-school hip-hop and house sampler after the SP-404 and the PO-33: two song samples and a 16-pad kit, up to 32 chops a song, a 64-step sequencer, patterns and a song arrangement. Built on Felucca.

The companion to the GammaWave desktop synth: four industrial distortions, vowel and scream filters, an FFT spectrogram, a four-track tape deck screen and a song generator with 49 genres, trap and drill too.

A pocket arranger after the QY70: pick a style, play three keys for a chord and a band of eight follows, songs from sections, General MIDI sounds from Sonivox EAS, and a General MIDI module over MIDI in.
A first instrument for toddlers: random key bashing and knob turning are rewarded with dancing animated pets and little musical sequences. Press a key, any key.
A music toy for little children: 63 cartoon friends, every key in tune, chords, strumming, songs to follow and an ear game, notes on a staff, a volume cap for small ears.

An eight-track groovebox for sound design: thirteen synth engines, struck percussion and 33 drum machines after the Machinedrum, on an influence grid where any track can trigger, excite or modulate any other.
A synth after the Roland S-1 and the SH-101: a punchy sub-oscillator, a resonant filter, bass and lead sounds and hands-on controls for playing live. Built on OberVave.

A string ensemble in the spirit of the late-70s machines, grown out of OberVave: divide-down keyers with 16', 8' and 4' footages, register filters, a BBD ensemble and a phaser per sound. Now on four tracks with a mixer, delay, reverb, drive, a master and the step sequencer.
The Commodore 64's SID chip, twice for six voices. Its web app edits patches and takes them straight from .sid game music files.
Turns the FM-1 into a C64 SID machine: two SIDs (6581 and 8580) with the chip's character dialled in, a GoatTracker 2 compatible tracker and step sequencer, and a live instrument to play over a song.

Six tracks of synths and drums with a groovebox's workflow: fourteen engines, a 64-step sequencer with chords, ratchets, trig conditions and locks, songs, PERFORM with scenes, six themes and a browser editor; FM6 sounds built from scratch on the unit. Built on Felucca, with most of Felucca 1.6.1's work brought over (the second core, MIDI LEARN, INSERT); Felucca's sounds and projects load. Also runs on the SMK-37 Pro.
A live groovebox: tracks, layers, a step sequencer, song mode, punch-in effects and samples, played on the FM-1 in real time.
SLOOP 2.4 with up to twelve DX7 voice banks, kept and named in the editor, presets by kind. Test builds: back up first.
SLOOP with a visual four-operator FM engine after Floyd Steinberg's 4-OP idea: an ADSR per operator, seven pages, a live oscilloscope that draws the envelopes as you play.
SLOOP's live workflow with Dexed's DX7 engine and 128 steps a track: six operators, 32 algorithms, your own .syx banks, every voice edited on the FM-1, FM drums you program.

A 12-voice wavetable synth: two oscillators a voice, a resonant filter, two envelopes, an LFO, four effects, an arpeggiator and two step sequencers for chords and counterpoint; load your own Serum, WaveEdit, Ableton or Surge tables.

Generative music on four tracks: each plays its own steps, an arpeggio or one of 13 generators (Turing, Euclid, Markov, Constellation, Chord and more), and the tracks evolve, follow and modulate each other. EVOLVE and FORM grow phrases into songs; 16 mod cords connect anything. A Melodee fork.
Six tracks for live ambient and experimental music: three synth engines, patches generated by algorithm, free-length loops with up to ten overdubs each, a granulator, filters and a lush reverb.
A ten-track groovebox where any engine plays on any track: kicks, 909 and 808 voices, the 303, sixteen clips a track, scatter effects and four master knobs you assign. Built on X0X.
Generative music built on Felucca: composer profiles write the music as it plays, you steer them. A work in progress.

Generative ambient and drone: Immaculate Permutation rolls an arrangement in one key, a pad, a sequence and a chord arpeggio under a fourth voice for your hands. Keep a sermon you like, evolve it, or reveal another.

An orbiting overtone synth: four corners of two overtone generators each, a sun on a path and a moon around it decide how much of each you hear; the knobs shape the selected planet. Made for the SMK-37, here its FM-1 build. After the Beetlecrab Vector.
Felucca played from an Arturia MiniLab 3: track faders, a DJ filter, momentary effect pads; 32 patches a bank, 12 evolving songs, revoiced 808 and CR78 kits.
Winamp 2.x on the FM-1, built on SLOOP: your sounds as a playlist, four tracks you record as loops, effects on sliders and a visualizer made of lines. The real firmware plays in a 3D simulator first.
A groovebox: 909 and 808 drums, two 303s with TB-3PO, a breakbeat generator and song mode.
X0X remixed after The Orb: banks and patterns reordered live per voice, Grids MAP and EUCLID drum generation, an extended TB-3PO with 22 scales and a morphing 303 waveform. Built on X0X.

Ambient as a living window: cherry petals on a river, koi in a pond, fireflies under a real moon, and every movement a note. Set it down and let it play; the keys play along, the knobs shape the scene.

A 12-bit sampler after the E-mu SP-1200: sample on the FM-1 itself (a computer or phone plays into it over USB) or in the browser (mic, line-in or a file), and it plays on its own. Gritty and unsmoothed, with loops and songs.
